Load a palette in scale_*_manual()

Source: R/spal.R
spal.Rd

spal() is a derivation of a palette-loading function in an R package I used to use quite regularly. Its intended use is interacting with ggplot2 functions like scale_fill_manual and scale_color_manual (in particular, the values argument). Herein, you can change the default ggplot2 colors used.

Usage

spal(
  palette,
  n = NULL,
  even = TRUE,
  d.mid = "#F7F7F7",
  exp = FALSE,
  lambda = 1.25
)

Arguments

palette

a label coinciding with a value in the color column of the steve_hex data frame

n

a mostly optional argument for how many colors you want. Defaults to NULL.

even

logical, defaults to TRUE, used internally for diverging palettes.

d.mid

a valid hex code coinciding with a color that should serve as the middle color in a palette with an odd-numbered length. Applicable only to diverging palettes. Default value here is "white" (#f7f7f7), a color slightly

exp

logical, defaults to FALSE, and applicable only to sequential palettes. If FALSE, palettes whiten by consistent amount each time across the range of colors (maximum: 9). If TRUE, palettes whiten as an exponential decay factor.

lambda

the parameter governing the rate of decay. Called only when exp is TRUE. Higher values mean a faster rate of decay.

Value

spal() returns a character vector of hex codes to use as a palette in manually supplying colors to adjust the fill or color of a plot made by ggplot2.

Details

Color palettes available are "d-suFB", "d-suBF", "d-suBR","d-suRB", "d-suBO", "d-suOB", "d-suFW", "d-suWF", "s-suB", "s-suF", "s-suO", "s-suR", "q-supair", "q-OI", "q-google", "q-ibm", "q-wong", "q-tol", "q-sciencespo", "q-dataroots", and "q-martel".

The n argument must be specified for sequential palettes and really should be specified for diverging palettes. If not, diverging palettes run the risk of being indistinguishable from sequential palettes.

Exponential decays are mostly experimental. I don't even know how much I would use this function. Use as you see fit. Exponential decays are min-max transformed to start at 1 and end at 1/n before applying the whitening factor to lighten_hex().

Description of Color Palettes

NameDescription
d-suFBdiverging palette, ranging from Stockholm University "Fire" to Stockholm University "Blue"
d-suBFdiverging palette, ranging from Stockholm University "Blue" to Stockholm University "Fire"
d-suBRdiverging palette, ranging from Stockholm University "Blue" to Stockholm University "Red"
d-suRBdiverging palette, ranging from Stockholm University "Red" to Stockholm University "Blue"
d-suBOdiverging palette, ranging from Stockholm University "Blue" to Stockholm University "Olive"
d-suOBdiverging palette, ranging from Stockholm University "Olive" to Stockholm University "Blue"
d-suFWdiverging palette, ranging from Stockholm University "Fire" to Stockholm University "Water"
d-suWFdiverging palette, ranging from Stockholm University "Water" to Stockholm University "Fire"
s-suBsequential palette, in shades of Stockholm University "Blue"
s-suFsequential palette, in shades of Stockholm University "Fire"
s-suOsequential palette, in shades of Stockholm University "Olive"
s-suRsequential palette, in shades of Stockholm University "Red"
s-suSsequential palette, in shades of Stockholm University "Sky"
s-suWsequential palette, in shades of Stockholm University "Water"
q-supairqualitative palette, using colors pairs of Stockholm University's template
q-OIqualitative palette, Okabe-Ito (Colorbind Friendly)
q-googlequalitative palette, using Google colors
q-ibmqualitative palette, using IBM Design Colorblind Safe Palette
q-wongqualitative palette, using Wong Colorblind Safe Palette
q-tolmqualitative palette, using Paul Tol's Muted Qualitative Palette
q-sciencespoqualitative palette, using Sciences-Po's Médialab (hard)
q-datarootsqualitative palette, paired, using Dataroots' colors
q-martelqualitative palette, using a palette of colors inspired by Rick Martel

Author

Steven V. Miller

Examples


spal("q-martel")
#> [1] "#e04892" "#411e65" "#70c6df" "#a01f19" "#000000"
spal("d-suBO")
#> [1] "#002f5f" "#3F6387" "#A5B6C7" "#CCD5DF" "#F7F7F7" "#ECEDE1" "#DEE0CB"
#> [8] "#BABD90" "#a3a86b"
spal("s-suB", n = 5)
#> [1] "#002f5f" "#32587E" "#66829F" "#99ABBF" "#CCD5DF"
